stats.label: of Falls Occur in the Bathroom

problem.heading: Why Existing Solutions Fall Short
problem.body: Bathing is one of the riskiest daily activities for older adults. Wet surfaces, tight space, and the repeated effort of lowering and raising the body make showers and tubs a high fall risk. Most shower chairs and transfer benches only give the user a fixed place to sit. They help with sitting, but not with moving: turning, reaching, shifting position, or transferring in and out. As a result, many seniors either bathe unsafely on their own, avoid bathing, or rely on a caregiver for tasks they could do themselves, which costs them privacy, dignity, and confidence. For users with very limited mobility, the equipment also makes the caregiver's job harder, since the cramped, wet space and fixed seating limit access and force awkward positions for both people. Lightweight or lower-grade materials add to the problem when users and caregivers need to trust the equipment to hold up under load and moisture.

mission.heading: What Movara Is Built to Do
mission.body: Movara is a shower seating and transfer system designed to make standing up and sitting down safer, and to give users more ways to move so they can bathe independently and privately for as long as possible. For users who need more help, Movara gives a PSW or caregiver a more stable, accessible, and convenient setup. Built from stronger, higher-quality materials, Movara aims to restore dignity and confidence while keeping safety first.

goals.heading: What Movara Sets Out to Achieve
items: Reduce fall risk during stand-to-sit and sit-to-stand in the shower.
Let more users bathe independently through added planes of movement and an elevated transfer system.
Make assisted bathing easier and safer for both the user and the caregiver.
Use durable, high-strength materials users and caregivers can trust.

differentiation.heading: How Movara Differentiates from Existing Products
differentiation.body: Movara's real differences are assisted vertical movement while seated (eccentric and concentric), travel along the tub's length, and the build strength.

mechanisms.title: Vertical Movement While Seated
mechanisms.subtitle: Rotating Pneumatic Seat Base
mechanisms.description: Unlike any existing transfer bench, Movara provides active vertical assistance while the user is seated — supporting both the downward (eccentric) and upward (concentric) phases of the sit-to-stand transition through a pneumatic mechanism.

mechanisms.title: Travel Along the Tub's Length
mechanisms.subtitle: Longitudinal Rail System
mechanisms.description: A longitudinal rail system allows the seat to travel along the full length of the bathtub, enabling users to position themselves under the showerhead or over the drain — eliminating the need to reach or stretch dangerously.

items.description: The rail lock is now default-locked. A spring-loaded pin seated in detents along the rail holds the frame in position at all times. The user releases it by squeezing a hand lever, and it re-locks the moment they let go. This directly addresses the scenario — raised in interviews — where a seated user inadvertently releases the frame, mirroring the concern about wheelchairs moving when brakes are forgotten. The same default-lock logic was applied to the height adjustment mechanism: non-negotiable for safe operation.

movements.heading: Four Planes of Movement. One Unified System.
movements.intro: The Movara transfer bench was engineered around a biomechanically informed movement model — combining four distinct planes of motion into a single, integrated assistive device.

cards.title: Lateral Transfer
cards.description: The seat slides across the full width of the frame, allowing the user to transition from outside the tub to inside with a smooth, guided, controlled movement. Eliminates the step-over hazard.

cards.title: Longitudinal Positioning
cards.description: Back-and-forth movement along the length of the bathtub allows users to position themselves precisely under the shower or over the drain, addressing the full bathing space.

cards.title: Elevation & Depression
cards.description: Adjustable seat height assists with eccentric and concentric muscle loading, reducing strain during sit-to-stand transitions and compensating for varying bathtub wall heights.

cards.title: 180° Rotation
cards.description: A mechanically limited rotation of up to 180° enables users to pivot toward the showerhead, faucets, grab bars, or caregivers — drastically expanding the functional reach envelope.

cad_gallery.heading: Precision-Engineered in Autodesk Fusion
cad_gallery.body: Every component of the Movara transfer bench was modelled in Autodesk Fusion, with iterative design revisions driven by physical testing outcomes, ergonomic analysis, and professional feedback. For the two animation clips, view them as looping silent clips to best appreciate the mechanism motion.

why_it_matters.heading: Engineering That Serves Human Dignity
why_it_matters.body: Beyond the mechanical specifications, the Movara project represents a commitment to human-centred engineering — designing systems that extend independence, reduce caregiver burden, and restore dignity in everyday moments. For the aging population, this is not a luxury; it is a necessity.
